title: Cap each creature at 3 a night? It makes nights varied, but the end of the night goes quiet
body:
What you'd see: today a night can pile up one kind. In 8 four-player test nights one night sent 12 Cinder Hounds, so a crew meets the same threat again and again. The other side is the pacing note 874 wants fixed: you want encounters to grow more frequent as the night goes on.

What was built: Nell's PR #1285 (queue #590, note 863) turns on the cap you chose on 19 Oct: no kind more than 3 a night (the Knotter 2), and a hound pack counts once. It's a draft with merge conflicts.

Measured, 8 nights, 4 bots: creatures a night 22.6 → 18.0; the most of one kind 12 → 3; distance, deliveries and cars lost unchanged. But car fires from hound packs a night rose from 0.5 to 8.75, and in a 20-minute test the director's sends by thirds went 3/7/9 → 4/7/0: the last third of the night goes quiet, because the capped kinds are used up by then.

Decision: should #1285 merge? Note 874 recommends merging it before the pacing items #608 and #612 start, with #612 then answering the pack fires and the quiet end.

Default meanwhile: agents build the pacing items assuming #1285 merges, and #612 owns fixing the pack fires. Nothing merges until you answer.

options.label: Merge #1285 now
options.detail: Variety up: no kind past 3. Hound-pack car fires rise ~17x until #612 answers them; the night's last third is quiet until #608 refills it. Recommended by note 874.

options.label: Hold it until the pacing work lands
options.detail: Nights stay as today (piles of one kind, a busier end). #608/#612 build around the old behaviour, and #1285 is redone after.

options.label: Merge with a higher cap (4 or 5)
options.detail: Less quiet at the end, less variety. Nell re-measures first; costs a few days.
